full_judgment:
3. Against the aforesaid proceeding, predecessors of the writ-respondents, filed Title Suit No. 34 of 1972 in the Court of  the then Munsif, Third Court, Dhaka, who by his judgment and decree dated 31.03.1976 decreed the suit . 

 8. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates, the impugned judgment and order and other papers on record. The High Court Division came to a finding that the then learned Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka, decreed Title Suit No. 176 of 1967 for specific performance of contract in respect of the disputed properties and that the decree was put to execution in Title Execution Case No. 19 of 1967 and that the deed of sale was executed and registered through the executing Court. The High Court Division also came to a finding that since the decree was passed by a competent Court and since the deed of sale was executed and registered by the Court itself and since possession of the writ-petitioners had been affirmed in the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 34 of 1972 of the Second Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka, the suit properties could not be included in the list of Vested Properties. The High Court Division observed that possession of the writ-petitioners in the suit land was not denied. Therefore, the High Court Division concluded that it was the legitimate right of the petitioners to get the suit properties released front the list of Vested Properties for avoiding future complications.
